messages:
maria_support: FYI customer 'AcmeTools' complaining about high p99 latency. Console shows region badge EU-West for their workspace, but their request logs show serving region us-east-1. They see ~220ms extra RTT. request_id=req_1a2b3c

sam_eng: ugh. do we have a repro? any request headers or example curl?

maria_support: pasted the curl they ran: 
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response headers snippet they pasted: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: req_1a2b3c
x-serving-region: us-east-1
x-console-region: eu-west-1
content-type: application/json
```

oliver_infra: ok that header is the smoking gun - our router emitted x-serving-region=us-east-1 (means served from us-east pool) while console metadata still flags the workspace as eu-west primary. Likely fallback routing kicked in. any recent capacity events? :thinking:

janet_sre: checking infra incidents... router logs show a transient capacity shortage in eu-west at 2024-11-04T14:02:xxZ and automatic fallback to us-east was enabled for latency policy. It should be surfaced in Console -> Routing History but I don't see a matching entry.

maria_support: customer says this happened repeatedly for an hour starting ~14:02 UTC. They got billed for tokens as usual but saw higher latency and complained about cross-region data flow (privacy concern). They want a breakdown and whether billing was charged at eu-west or us-east rates.

kevin_billing: billing uses cheapest-conforming region pricing per serving region tag. If x-serving-region is us-east-1 then cost applied to us-east SKU. We need to confirm logs for that timeframe to be sure. I can run a ledger query if you give me the request ids or timeframe.

sam_eng: to repro locally, I tried hitting their workspace with a short run but my requests stayed in eu-west. I can force a failover by simulating high queue depth. oliver, can you share the router policy code that decides fallback?

oliver_infra: pasted minimal config: 
```
route_policy {
  primary: eu-west-1
  fallback: [us-east-1, eu-central-1]
  trigger: capacity_threshold=0.85
  ttl: 300s
}
```
Behavior: if primary queues > threshold then route to first fallback. It logs an event and emits x-serving-region header. The console expects those events from 'route-event-stream' but apparently the consumer failed for that window.

janet_sre: found the consumer crash in kibana: consumer pod restarted at 14:02:11Z due to oom. Events from 14:02:11 -> 14:12:00Z were missed. Router didn't stop routing to fallback, but Console didn't ingest the events so workspace badge kept showing eu-west.

maria_support: customer-facing summary I drafted: "We routed your requests to a fallback region (us-east-1) during a brief capacity pressure in eu-west. Due to an internal ingestion outage, the Console incorrectly showed eu-west as the active region. We apologize for the confusion and the latency impact. We're reviewing the ingest consumer and we will share a billing reconciliation." Thoughts?

kevin_billing: fine, but include that billing will be reconciled if there was any anomalous charge. I'll run ledger query for 2024-11-04 14:00-15:00 UTC and follow up.

sam_eng: short-term mitigation: add an additional explicit header that Console can read directly from the router response in the UI for live requests (fallthrough visibility). e.g., expose x-live-serving-region in request inspector. Long-term: make event ingestion async with disk-backed buffer to survive consumer restarts.

oliver_infra: created infra ticket INF-4821 to add disk-backed buffer and increase consumer resources. Also opened hotfix PR to surface x-serving-region in Console request logs: https://git.redwood/infraproj/pull/542 (hotfix branch).

routing-bot: INF-4821 assigned to oliver_infra, priority P1, due 2024-11-08.

janet_sre: action items: (1) kevin run billing reconciliation (2) oliver roll hotfix to Console to show x-serving-region (3) infra team increase consumer mem and add buffer (4) support send customer note + temp mitigation steps. I'll own postmortem.

maria_support: sending the message to customer now. I'll include request ids and expected timeline. tagging @kevin_billing for recon. :thumbsup:

kevin_billing: got request window. running queries now, will post findings in this thread when done.

sam_eng: small repro snippet for others to test: 
```
# simulate queue pressure
ab -n 1000 -c 100 -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Note: don't run against prod without approval.

maria_support: thanks all. keeping thread open until billing + hotfix deployed.

routing-bot: hotfix-deploy status: queued -> in_progress at 2024-11-05T09:15:00Z

oliver_infra: hotfix merged and deployed to staging. will schedule prod deploy tonight 02:00 UTC.

kevin_billing: ledger audit complete. 452 requests in window were served from us-east and billed at us-east rates. Refund/adjustment required for 0 requests (pricing parity applied) — customer won't be charged extra. Posting audit: ledger_query_id=lg_77a9b0.

maria_support: customer updated: they appreciate transparency, no extra charge, but want an SLA note about cross-region routing. I've moved to 'escalated' and will coordinate legal if they request a formal amendment.

janet_sre: postmortem scheduled for Friday 2024-11-08 16:00 UTC. I'll include timeline, root cause (OOM consumer), and remediation plan. Closing thread once postmortem is published.

maria_support: closing for now, will reopen if customer pushes. :white_check_mark:
